name: MM-BrowseComp
intro: MM-BrowseComp是一个全面的多模态深度研究基准，旨在评估智能体通过浏览和推理多模态网页内容来解决复杂问题的能力。该基准包含224个具有挑战性的多跳问题，每个问题的解决方案都特意设计为需要理解图像或视频模态中的内容。评估结果显示，即使是OpenAI o3等最强模型也未能超过30%的准确率，凸显了当前模型在多模态理解和推理方面的不足。该基准还提供了经过验证的清单，用于细粒度分析多模态依赖性和推理路径。
org: ByteDance, Nanjing University, M-A-P, CASIA, Zhejiang University
build_method: 专家反向构题, 三阶段验证, 不可约清单标注
metric: 整体准确率, 严格准确率, 平均清单得分
modality: 文本, 图像, 视频, 多模态
eval_feature: 加密防污染, 清单过程评估, 版本钉住
scale: 论文 v1：224 道题、22 个子任务；论文后另有 400 题扩展
build_method_en: Expert Reverse Construction, Three-stage Validation, Irreducible Checklist Annotation
eval_feature_en: Encrypted Anti-contamination, Checklist Process Evaluation, Version-pinned Release
intro_en: MM-BrowseComp is a comprehensive multimodal deep research benchmark designed to evaluate agents' ability to solve complex problems by browsing and reasoning over multimodal web content. The benchmark includes 224 challenging multi-hop questions, each requiring understanding of content in image or video modalities. Evaluation results show that even top models like OpenAI o3 fail to exceed 30% accuracy, highlighting current limitations in multimodal understanding and reasoning. The benchmark also provides a validated checklist for fine-grained analysis of multimodal dependencies and reasoning paths.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2508.13186v1 (submitted 2025-08-14), the first public official data-and-code commit 5f5298cd0e84ac511ad1cda3840cef73773661cc (2025-08-20), and current audit commit cf82a2390aa7a7ed3d96f72969d22548eff3e101 (2026-01-04). Paper v1 is fixed at 224 unique rows across 22 subtasks and five categories; the later data/MMBrowseComp_400.jsonl has 400 unique IDs, retains all 224 paper IDs, and adds 176 IDs, so it is documented only as post-paper drift. Paper construction uses more than 20 master's/PhD AI researchers, reverse construction from authoritative facts, mandatory visual evidence absent from text sources, an irreducible sequential checklist, single-attempt Gemini-2.5-Pro/GPT-4o web-search failure, a five-minute unfamiliar-annotator gate, alternative-answer search, and temporal constraints when needed. Validation is pilot calibration, full construction plus secondary review, then tool-dependency and factual verification; 300 candidates become 161 direct accepts, 63 revisions, and 76 discards. The paper reports 57% image-bearing questions, while the first public 224-row file contains 130/224 (58.0%) rows with non-empty images. The pinned 224-row release has the exact fields id, question, images, answer, canary, checklist, checklist_property, category, source, subtask, and level; question, answer, and checklist are encrypted with a per-row canary, and the official README says not to publish decrypted plaintext. At audit commit cf82a23 the README displays an MIT badge but no LICENSE file exists, so the diagram does not infer a separate dataset license; there is no official submission server or leaderboard. Paper Table 1 is Pass@1: full 224 for tool-free and official tool-enabled services, but a uniformly subtask-sampled 54-item subset for costly open-source agents. All models receive the answer-plus-roadmap wrapper and GPT-4o-2024-11-20 judges question, reference answer, checklist, and generated answer. The released judge prompt receives no original images; its parser extracts CHECKLIST_SCORE, CHECKLIST_RESULT, and OVERALL_CORRECTNESS, but only a missing OVERALL field sets parser_error. The released aggregate covers only the current run: pre-judge failures and --skip_evaluated files are excluded; an exhausted judge call still carries raw_judge_response: null and remains in the OA/SA denominator; AVG CS divides only by items with numeric c/t. Paper definitions remain OA final-answer correctness, SA final answer plus all checks, and mean checklist completion; o3 reports 29.02 OA, 19.64 SA, and 36.49 AVG CS. The separate 16-run Agent-R1 test-time-scaling study uses majority, confidence-weighted, and Best-of-N aggregation and is not folded into Table 1 Pass@1. Reproduction gaps retained in the audit branch: no exact paper-time repository commit, the six-days-later scripts are a generic baseline rather than the complete Table 1 multi-framework harness, no 54-item subset IDs or sampling seed are released, and the conclusion says 244 while the body, tables, and released paper dataset say 224. Formal publication evidence [site-a11l-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 1885×2001 (English) and 1885×2001 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 1883×1999 and 1883×1999. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
